messages:
Sasha (customer): Hey team — after switching to the reserved pool last night we're seeing a spike of 429s for a subset of calls when clients burst. SLA says 99.9% p99 latency and no more than 0.5% errors; we're currently seeing 3-4% 429s during the 30s window after a deploy.

Sasha (customer): Details: reserved_pool_id=rp-az1-42, model=gpt-large-v2, pool_capacity=200 concurrent connections, workers=8 (A100). Error example: response headers show X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and body {"error":"rate_limited"}. Happened around 2026-03-14T22:12Z.

Maya (support): Sorry you're hitting that, Sasha — we'll dig in. Quick Qs: are the 429s per-route or across all endpoints? Are you sending large batches (many tokens) or many small requests?

Sasha (customer): Mostly small requests (250-400 tokens each), high QPS for a short ramp during our marketing event. It's across text generation and chat routes, not embeddings.

Maya (support): Got it. Can you run this reproduce curl so we can capture request-id and response headers?

Maya (support): ```bash
for i in $(seq 1 200); do 
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDSHIFT_API_KEY" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-large-v2","input":"hi","max_tokens":300}' \
    https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.05
done
```

Sasha (customer): ran it — sample response headers we captured: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 25
x-redwood-pool: rp-az1-42
X-Request-ID: req-0a12bc34
```

Maya (support): Thanks. That X-RateLimit-Limit=1200 likely reflects a global per-minute token/QPS cap the controller enforces. I'm going to pull the pool config and routing policy now.

Jonah (eng-oncall): Jumping in. First pass: two possible failure modes — 1) reserved pool is hitting its configured throughput cap (tokens/sec or requests/sec depending on config) and the shaping policy is rejecting; 2) short-burst window miscalculation where the burst credit bucket is drained and not refilling quickly enough.

Jonah (eng-oncall): Can you provide a sample request-id (X-Request-ID) from a 429 response? I want to cross-check traces.

Sasha (customer): X-Request-ID: req-0a12bc34 (from the previous header).

Jonah (eng-oncall): Thanks. Running trace lookup: `curl -s "https://internal-traces.redwood/api/trace?req=req-0a12bc34"` returned this summary: "throttle at rate_limiter:reserve_pool_shaper (remaining=0, refill_rate=20r/s, burst_capacity=40)"

Jonah (eng-oncall): That indicates the pool is set to refill at 20 req/s with burst 40 — your event ramp exceeds that and the shaper is enforcing. SLA alignment note: Dedicated SLA is for steady-state throughput and latency; short bursts are subject to reserved_pool.burst_capacity.

Tariq (dedicated-ops): FYI we recently shipped a change to the controller that tightened the default shaping window; some pools created before the change kept older burst settings but pools recreated via API got the new conservative defaults. rp-az1-42 was created last year and might have been migrated with stricter limits.

Tariq (dedicated-ops): Workarounds: 
- Increase reserved_pool.burst_capacity and/or refill_rate for rp-az1-42 (temporary).
- Enable burst_buffer:true in pool config to allow short spikes to queue rather than 429.
- Add a short client-side exponential backoff/retry for 429s (recommended).

Maya (support): To change config we need confirmation from account owner. If you want us to escalate, please confirm you'd like refill_rate bump to 80r/s and burst_capacity to 200 for the 6-hour window of the campaign.

Sasha (customer): Please bump for 6 hours. We can revert after. Also want to understand long-term: we're paying for a 200-concurrency dedicated pool — why are we capped like this?

Jonah (eng-oncall): Two things: capacity (concurrency/workers) controls model decode parallelism; shaping controls request ingress to keep latency SLOs. If you push too many small requests very fast, the shaper limits to preserve latency for other tenants on same physical node unless you have isolated capacity. For true unlimited burst you need dedicated-isolated reservations (different SKU) or pre-allocated burst credits.

Maya (support): For the immediate fix I can open a config-change ticket with dedicated-ops and mark P2 (customer-facing outage risk). Tariq, do you want the temporary bump?

Tariq (dedicated-ops): Yes, I'll apply the temporary bump. I'll also check controller migration history for rp-az1-42 and whether the pool was auto-migrated to new defaults.

Priya (acctmgmt): Looping in billing — note that increasing refill_rate will increase token consumption and could push toward a higher committed usage tier. Sasha, want me to estimate incremental spend for 6h at expected QPS?

Sasha (customer): Yes please, estimate would be great. We have a budget for the event but want to avoid surprise charges.

billing-bot: automated alert — reserved_pool rp-az1-42 reached 95% of hourly quota at 2026-03-14T22:15Z (usage=95k tokens/hr, quota=100k tokens/hr). Invoice note will reflect additional consumption beyond committed usage.

Priya (acctmgmt): Quick calc: if we set refill_rate to 80r/s and average tokens/request ~300, that's ~24k tokens/min => ~1.44M tokens/hour. Compared to your current quota (100k tokens/hr) it will be a large overage. Suggest setting a temporary treaty: grant a 6-hour burst waiver or upgrade commitment for the campaign window.

Sasha (customer): Ok—please apply the waiver for 6 hours. We approve.

Maya (support): Action items so far:
- (M1) Tariq to apply temporary bump to refill_rate=80r/s, burst_capacity=200 for rp-az1-42 for 6 hours (ETA 10m)
- (M2) Jonah to monitor rate-limiter metrics and p99 latency for the pool during window
- (M3) Priya to create a billing waiver/ticket for the 6-hour overage
- (M4) Support to provide client-side retry recommendation and sample backoff code

Jonah (eng-oncall): I'll share a quick monitoring query to watch refill and consumed credits: 
```
sum(rate(rate_limiter_tokens_consumed_total{pool="rp-az1-42"}[30s])) by (instance)
sum(rate(rate_limiter_refill_total{pool="rp-az1-42"}[30s])) by (instance)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{pool="rp-az1-42"}[5m])) by (le))
```

Tariq (dedicated-ops): Applied temporary bump at 1769004405 — refill_rate -> 80r/s, burst_capacity -> 200, burst_buffer=true. Monitor and report any oddness. (reaction :fire:)

Maya (support): Please re-run the reproduce script from earlier and attach new response headers.

Sasha (customer): Reran it. Sample headers now: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-RateLimit-Limit: 4800
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 4792
X-Request-ID: req-0a12ff99
x-redwood-pool: rp-az1-42
```

Sasha (customer): p99 latency looks within SLA now, and 429s dropped to ~0.2% over 10 minutes. Thanks.

Maya (support): Great — closing immediate incident. Follow-ups:
- (F1) Eng to review pool migration and default shaping logic to ensure pools with committed capacity get appropriate defaults.
- (F2) Product to clarify docs on burst behavior for Dedicated and add sample client retry/backoff patterns.
- (F3) Billing to confirm waiver issuance and provide invoice impact.

Priya (acctmgmt): I've filed the waiver and will follow up with an approval reference ID in the ticket.

Jonah (eng-oncall): Long-term suggestion: consider reserving an isolated burst SKU for predictable events (separate from shared reserved pools) or coordinate a scheduled pre-warm where we temporarily increase refill and commit tokens in advance.

Sasha (customer): Appreciate quick turnaround — we'll take the retry pattern and discuss long-term burst SKU with our solutions engineer.

Maya (support): Closing thread for now — reopening if anything else crops up. (reaction :thumbsup:)
